description: Organization consent and governance history. For every "consents.accept" entry an implementation MUST accept the consent against the stated act and person control head and derive exactly the expected body; it MUST refuse every "consents.reject" entry. For every "governance.accept" entry it MUST replay the governance log, using only the supplied identity logs to establish person control heads, and derive exactly the expected heads; it MUST refuse every "governance.reject" entry. All keys and identities here are published test material.

rules.transition_digest: SHA-256(UTF-8(canonical JSON of {"domain":transition_domain,"body":transition})) as lowercase hex; it is what consents name and what the next head's previous_digest is.
rules.head_digest: SHA-256(UTF-8(canonical JSON of the governance head)) as lowercase hex, with no domain, like a person control head.
rules.consent_head: A consent's head_digest is the digest of the person control head whose operational quorum signs it; the verifier establishes that head from the person's identity log or, at acceptance, from a fresh resolution.

accept.why: a controller consents to the genesis under their current head, signed by their operational key
a consent signed under an earlier head of a person who has since rotated: valid under that head, which a replay verifier finds in the person's log

reject.why: signed by the person's recovery key: recovery keys are not business signers
signed by a stranger
signed by a retired operational key, checked under the current head
the head digest names a head the person never had
verified under another person's head
consent to a different digest
consent to a transition presented as consent to the genesis
consent for another organization
a body altered after signing
a window longer than the organization ceremony bound
a consent signed under the transition domain
an extra member
the same key signing twice
no signatures

accept.why: a genesis with two controllers, each consenting under their current head
a controller joins with a raised threshold, then the founder leaves: every head replays from the consents alone
the same history verified with only the logs of the people who ever consented

reject.why: a genesis consent missing: every initial controller must consent
a genesis consent from a person who is not an initial controller
a person's identity log withheld: their head cannot be established, so their consent fails
a transition consented to only by the added controller: the current quorum is missing
a transition adding a controller who did not consent
a transition consented to by one of three where the threshold is two
a transition naming a governance digest that is not the current head
a skipped sequence
entries reordered
a transition body altered after the consents were signed
a consent under a fabricated person head
a transition whose controllers are not in ascending order
a transition that changes nothing
a genesis consent reused as consent to a transition
an unknown format
an extra top-level member
